testOnlyKeys: Every secret here (testOnlySecrets, the signing keys behind every signature) is a synthetic TEST ONLY scalar: keccak256 of a label containing 'TEST ONLY', reduced, or, in the passkey section, derived by the passkey derivation from TEST ONLY PRF fixtures (32 x 0x00 / 32 x 0x01, or SHA-256 of a 'TEST ONLY' label). Never use them for anything else. Networks, corridors, nonces and digests are fixtures.

recipientMessage.decided: 2026-10-24/25 by the product owner; replaces the compatibility spike's provisional plain mod r
rule: d = the EIP-712 digest of the inner struct (keccak256(0x1901 || domainSeparator || hashStruct))
u = keccak256(P || d || 0x00) || keccak256(P || d || 0x01)
m = OS2IP(u[0:48]) mod r
the account signs m as a 32-byte big-endian field element under SchnorrAccount's scheme

schnorr.challenge: e = poseidon2([SCHNORR_CHALLENGE_DST, R.x, P.x, P.y, m]); accept iff P on curve, s != 0, e != 0, R = s*G + e*P != O
schnorr.signatureEncoding: s || e, 32 bytes each, big-endian (64 bytes); canonical s < q, e < r
schnorr.testOnlyNonce: the vectors' nonce k = OS2IP(sha512('xochi-spec TEST ONLY schnorr nonce' || sk || m)) mod q; any valid nonce verifies the same way

recipientMessage.tooling: The recipient's own tooling rebuilds the full typed preimage, computes d, applies the wrapper and signs m. It never signs a digest or field value supplied by Xochi.

reduction.name: (r + 1) * 2^128: truncation to 256 bits gives r + 1 (-> 1), wide gives 2^128
kmax * r (largest multiple of r below 2^384)

acknowledgements.domain: Domain (binding): every acknowledgement is a statement by the recipient about one binding, so it is scoped to that binding's environment, network and source chain. Primary type and purpose string separate the types inside the domain; a dedicated domain would add no separation those two do not.

BackupPersistenceAck.backupCommitment = keccak256(randomized encrypted backup bytes); backupFormatId = keccak256(UTF8("xochi.shielded.backup-format.v1")) = 0xe37c67f007c5a5bbebbc6c5b9aefd99f252b2cc121e3fc9a269801940f605348; neither value contains plaintext. This is the sealed-file format; passkey.backup.rule adds the passkey format and supersedes this rule for it

BackupPersistenceAck, SenderRegistrationAck and TokenRegistrationAck are enrollment acknowledgements: nonce / challengeExpiry equal the named RecipientBinding challenge members exactly; no second enrollment challenge is issued
PaymentReceiptAck nonce / challengeExpiry are a separate server-issued single-use receipt challenge and signing window
SenderRegistrationAck.registeredSenders: nonempty, strictly ascending (bytewise), each a nonzero in-field Aztec address
PaymentReceiptAck.amount: the exact credited BaseUnits, 0 < amount <= 2^128 - 1; blockNumber: decimal string on the wire

TokenRegistrationAck (xochi#753): aztecToken equals the binding's aztecToken; aztecTokenClassId and tokenImmutablesHash equal the verifier's trusted corridor record (oxideToken); each a nonzero in-field value. Required exactly when the corridor's token class is in oxideToken.oxideTokenClassIds

passkey.status: APPROVED: product-owner sign-off on departing from xochi#759's sealed backup received 2026-11-09; decided in epic xochi#833 (xochi-sdk#155). Rollout remains gated on PASSKEY-RECIPIENT.md's CSP and xochi.fi host prerequisites. Additive: every value outside this section is unchanged.
rule: prfInputs.first.value / prfInputs.second.value = SHA-256(UTF8(label)); the page passes those 32 raw bytes (never their hex text) as extensions.prf.eval.{first, second} in one ceremony (the browser hashes each again with the 'WebAuthn PRF' context before the authenticator sees it)
prf.first / prf.second = getClientExtensionResults().prf.results.{first, second}: each exactly 32 bytes, else prf_output_invalid; prf.second equal to prf.first: prf_output_invalid on prf.second
every HKDF below is HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869) with salt = hkdf.salt = UTF8("xochi.recipient.passkey.v1") and info = UTF8 of the hkdf.outputs entry's info string

secret = OS2IP(HKDF(prf.first, info = UTF8("xochi.recipient.passkey.v1/account-secret"), L = 64)) mod r; salt = OS2IP(HKDF(prf.first, info = UTF8("xochi.recipient.passkey.v1/account-salt"), L = 64)) mod r; either zero: derived_zero
wrapKey = HKDF(prf.second, info = UTF8("xochi.recipient.passkey.v1/wrap-key"), L = 32): the AES-256-GCM key of the PKW1 wrapped import
pxeStoreKey = HKDF(prf.second, info = UTF8("xochi.recipient.passkey.v1/pxe-store-key"), L = 32): the key of the browser's persisted encrypted PXE store; derived on every unlock, never persisted
version: only derivationVersion is accepted, else unsupported_version

account: stock SchnorrAccount (profile aztec-6.0.0), signing key = deriveMasterMessageSigningSecretKey(secret) (the MSSK_M master scalar), keys = deriveKeys(secret), salt = the derived salt, deployer = 0; one passkey is one recipient

derivations.prfSource: first = SHA-256(UTF8("TEST ONLY prf first")), second = SHA-256(UTF8("TEST ONLY prf second"))

rule: BackupPersistenceAck (type, purpose and struct unchanged) accepts two backupFormatId values: 0xe37c67f007c5a5bbebbc6c5b9aefd99f252b2cc121e3fc9a269801940f605348 (sealed file) and 0xfc8e02b9741f099f45fc73cf480359a580e322ceae9ca66d3964a987ad4517f2 (passkey); the format id is the mode. This supersedes acknowledgements.rules' sealed-file-only backupFormatId rule for the passkey format

passkey backupCommitment = keccak256(abi.encode(bytes32 commitmentTag, bytes32 credentialIdHash, bytes32 keccak256(UTF8(rpId)), uint32 derivationVersion)); credentialIdHash = keccak256(raw credential id), nonzero; rpId exactly 'xochi.fi' (rp_id_mismatch); derivationVersion exactly 1 (derivation_version_unsupported)

only a recipient whose keys derive from the passkey (profile mode 'passkey') may use the passkey format; an imported (PKW1) recipient keeps the sealed-file format and its keccak256(sealed backup bytes) commitment, since PKW1 is a device-local cache, not a backup
a verifier without a format expectation (absent or null) accepts only the sealed-file format (backup_format_mismatch); with one, the acknowledgement's format must equal it (subject_mismatch)
the commitment names the credential, never key material; nothing proves the passkey exists or is synced: the acknowledgement is the recipient's statement, as for the sealed file
